body.text: Beyond Classical Radar Limits

Most coverage of The Physics of Quantum Radar misses the structural details that actually matter in science. When you look closely at real-world evidence, clear patterns emerge that separate durable results from short-term noise.

Classical radar systems rely on broadcasting high-power microwave pulses and detecting coherent reflected echoes. Stealth aircraft defeat this mechanism through faceted radar-absorbent materials (RAM) and shape geometry which deflects reflections away from the receiver. Quantum radar supersedes this limitation using quantum illumination: generating entangled photon pairs where one photon serves as an internal idler and the second is beamed into the atmosphere as a signal probe.
Core Mechanisms of Quantum Illumination

items: Josephson Parametric Amplifiers: Superconducting circuits operating at millikelvin temperatures which split microwave pump photons into entangled signal-idler pairs.
Electro-Optomechanical Converters: Converting optical laser entanglement into microwave frequencies suitable for atmospheric propagation.
Quantum Correlated Reception: Measuring quantum discord and quantum state correlations between the stored idler and returning signal photons.
Jamming Immunity: Thermal electromagnetic noise and artificial jamming cannot spoof quantum entanglement signatures, isolating authentic target returns.

body.text: Surviving Atmospheric Decoherence

The fundamental challenge of quantum radar is atmospheric loss: rain, fog, and thermal photons rapidly degrade delicate quantum states. Yet, quantum illumination does not require the entanglement itself to survive the round trip. The initial entanglement grants a provable 3-to-6 dB signal-to-noise ratio advantage over classical illumination, sufficient to expose radar-invisible targets.
